blockers.title: Mandatory unpublished-allocation rollback conflicts with the accepted predecessor failure contract
blockers.finding: The current review mandate explicitly requires judging the current user requirement to roll back unpublished allocations. Revision01 instead intentionally retains every acquired lease, consumes capacity and allocation identities, retains any staged pins, and irreversibly closes Terminal. The first-new-allocation denial case retains 10 inherited frames; denial after acquiring user_stack would retain 11, and table-alias or later prepublication failure could retain all 12. PDE256 absence prevents USER exposure but is not restoration of allocation, capacity, pin or ledger state. A pure preflight refusal being effect-free does not satisfy rollback for a transaction that has already acquired unpublished frames. Accepted F1 v2:52,114-115 expressly requires the opposite failure disposition. This is a contract incompatibility, not a resource leak that the reviewer may silently waive.
blockers.smallest_in_scope_remedy: No implementation remedy is authorized under the simultaneous requirements. STOP implementation and obtain an explicit operator disposition that supersedes/withdraws the current unpublished-allocation rollback requirement in favor of bounded terminal retention. Alternatively, actual allocation rollback requires separately authorized predecessor failure-policy review/change; that is outside this F4-only scope. Do not add release/retry/unseal, call existing rollback-capable generic builders as a substitute, or rename retention rollback.
blockers.qualification: The proposed terminal-retention implementation itself is compatible with accepted F1 and fits the ceiling; it cannot satisfy the additional mandatory allocation-restoration requirement at the same time. Only an explicit change to that current requirement could permit proceeding without changing F1.

blockers.title: Ring0 RO fault oracle does not exclude SMAP as the cause
blockers.finding: Admission checks PAE/PSE/CET off but does not constrain CR4.SMAP or interpret EFLAGS.AC. The inherited F3/F2 profile checks do not constrain SMAP either. A CPL0 explicit data write to a present user-mode address with SMAP=1 and AC=0 faults independently of the leaf R/W permission; a protection/write supervisor #PF can therefore satisfy the stated code_write P/W-bit oracle even if the intended WP/RO causal proof is absent. Pinning a future qemu32 invocation or capturing raw registers is not an explicit fail-closed semantic check. SMEP independently controls supervisor instruction fetch from USER mappings even in non-PAE mode; there is no F4 instruction-fetch probe, so it must not be conflated with NX or a required CPL3 proof.
blockers.smallest_in_scope_remedy: Specify F4-local (not F2/F3 policy) admission and hardware evidence checks requiring observed CR4.SMAP=0, or select and fully evidence a bounded explicit AC override. The simpler fixed-profile remedy is SMAP=0 without changing any control register. Record/check SMEP and AC, request CPUID.7.0 feature words only if leaf0 permits it, and distinguish irrelevant SMEP for these data-only probes. Require a successful same-mode USER-stack read/write positive control before the RO write, then exact #PF vector14, CR2=0x40000000, P=1,W=1,U=0,RSVD=0,I/D=0 for the RO store. Keep this inside the existing ready/code_write scenarios and the same two new gates; do not add CPL3 or change F2/F3 profiles.

overall_reason: Current mandatory allocation-rollback requirement is incompatible with accepted terminal-retention policy; Ring0 fault proof additionally leaves SMAP causality unresolved. No approval with ambiguities.

checks.name: effective_PDE_PTE_semantics
checks.detail: Non-PAE 1024x1024 u32 entries, 4096-byte structures and leaves. P at both levels is required; USER effective only if both U bits are1; effective ordinary RW is their intersection and CR0.WP=1 applies to supervisor writes, subject to SMAP (B2). PDE256 P/RW/U with PTE0 P/U/RO and PTE1023 P/U/RW correctly yields the proposed map; software runtime marker is not a hardware right. PDE PS must remain0. No per-page NX in this mode.

checks.name: lease_authority_and_roles
checks.detail: Private move-only addr/id/domain tokens plus initialized same-domain live allocation ledger authenticate ownership. Coverage/reservation/history/free checks are stronger than not-free. Pins are physical lifetime protection, not ownership authentication or virtual lifetime. Design additionally excludes boot/kernel/MMIO/structure/duplicate/runtime roles and validates full writable supervisor identity aliases before writes. The F3 eight frames are already runtime-pinned; final F4 validation must validate their expected roles, not apply new-payload unpinned predicate to them.

checks.name: publication_ordering
checks.detail: A new leased table remains unreachable at raw PDE256=0 while exactly two leaves are populated. Permanent owning slots, runtime/structure pins and bitmap mirrors precede hardware publication; map inventory/accounting precede the last PDE store. Existing write_entry uses plain ptr::write, not volatile. The proposed F4 path must actually provide the promised compiler ordering/volatile publication mechanism and emitted ordering evidence; x86 store order alone cannot replace that. INVLPG must execute after publication with no CR3 switch and no fallible operation inside commit. No need to promote a predecessor supervisor PDE.

checks.name: kernel_isolation_and_physical_aliases
checks.detail: Only payload and user_stack physical frames may occur in effective USER leaves. The preflight must validate raw PDE/table inventory and pointer accessibility before dereferencing, then every present supervisor PTE and forbidden physical alias. Kernel image/metadata/descriptor/page structures/privileged stacks/MMIO remain supervisor-only at both levels; inherited supervisor RW identity aliases of USER payload are intentional cooperative Ring0 authority. Table structure pin excludes payload reuse. This is not hostile-Ring0, DMA, SMP or cross-process isolation.

checks.name: guards_layout_and_page_granularity
checks.detail: One PDE256 covers [0x40000000,0x40400000). Slot0 has both subpage code and RO data with identical permissions. PTE1..1022 absent; slot1022 is lower stack guard;1023 is stack. PDE257 absence provides an upper boundary without allocating another table. No independent writable-data page; no subpage protection; guard does not stop skipped-guard accesses, arbitrary overflow or physical-alias misuse. Unmapped range faults do not establish user privilege denial. Guard bytes and raw zero holes need actual guest capture.

After-commit failure retains a complete arena and must not report GREEN; it is not a rollback or successful request. Do not use no partial USER return as a capacity-restoration claim.

While Preparing, CLI, single-vCPU, no owner reentry/callbacks and continuous map/frame ownership protect the transaction; all guards released before GDT install or terminal output. Descriptor installation after unlock uses existing scalar snapshot access, not locks held through it.
